title: Inspect an xz stream and recover exact bytes
goal: Practice xz/xzcat, bounded memory/threads, container validation versus independent content checks.
challenge: Select and recover the correct small stream, prove independent expected bytes and retain the rejected candidate. Retain actual outputs/statuses and preserve originals; report reasoning through self-review, not a score.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/foundation-xz-evidence.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && umask 077; here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/foundation-xz-evidence.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700; }; fresh() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test ! -e "$1" && test ! -L "$1"; }; regular() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h "$1")" = learner:600:1; }; here && test "$(df -B1 --output=avail / | tail -1)" -ge 1073741824 && pwd
steps.explanation: Record this unique guest-only workspace. On Resume re-establish the recorded path/definitions; never overwrite another exercise.
steps.expected: Private learner-owned700 directory and observed1GiB free admission.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/source.txt" && fresh "$w/source.sha" && printf "caf\303\251\n" > source.txt && sha256sum source.txt > source.sha && test "$(wc -c < source.txt)" -le 65536 && fresh "$w/good.xz" && timeout -k 1s 10s xz --threads=1 --memlimit-compress=64MiB -1 -c source.txt > good.xz && timeout -k 1s 10s xz --list good.xz && timeout -k 1s 10s xz --memlimit-decompress=64MiB -t good.xz
steps.explanation: Keep the source using -c; one worker and small fixed input. Container integrity is neither authentication nor correct-content proof.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/restored.txt" && timeout -k 1s 10s xzcat --memlimit-decompress=64MiB good.xz > restored.txt && cmp source.txt restored.txt && sha256sum -c source.sha && fresh "$w/truncated.xz" && head -c 12 good.xz > truncated.xz
steps.explanation: Recover separately and compare independent original bytes; create only a tiny private damaged candidate.
steps.expected: Exact recovery and retained 12-byte rejected candidate.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/damaged.log" || return 19; if timeout -k 1s 10s xz --memlimit-decompress=64MiB -t truncated.xz > damaged.log 2>&1; then return 1; else test $? = 1 && test -s damaged.log && sha256sum -c source.sha; fi; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: Require actual damage refusal, not any earlier guard failure. Do not overwrite source or retained stream.
steps.expected: Container test rejects known truncated copy.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/low-partial.xz" && fresh "$w/low.log" || return 19; if timeout -k 1s 10s xz --threads=1 --memlimit-compress=1MiB --no-adjust -9 -c source.txt > low-partial.xz 2> low.log; then return 1; else test $? = 1 && grep -F "Memory usage limit is too low for the given filter setup." low.log && grep -F "The limit is 1 MiB." low.log && sha256sum -c source.sha; fi; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: This deliberate refusal tests requested resource setup without allocating the reported674MiB. --no-adjust prevents silent preset reduction.

hints: xz -t success is not authenticity or the correct report; avoid default source deletion and force overwrite.
Choose command scope deliberately; compare known bytes and actual statuses, not only a successful-looking display.
Retain before evidence; refuse collisions and restore exact policy state before leaving. Guest root can bypass guest-side guards.
review: I demonstrated the selected mode’s actual observations and retained an incorrect or incomplete case.
I preserved originals and can explain the reasoning and limitations; this records self-review, not automatic assessment.
I restored any changed default/zone and retained the exact workspace without touching unrelated files.
coverage: LPIC-1 active v5.0 partial103.2 xzcat and103.3 xz/unxz; limited LPIC-2 activev4.5 206.2 compression reinforcement only. Container validation is not correct-content/authenticity proof; no complete-objective credit.
